speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your hand tremors and recent memory issues, can you tell me if these symptoms have been getting worse over time or if they happen suddenly? Also, have you noticed any changes in your walking, balance, or speech?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful. To further characterize the tremor, does it become more pronounced when your hand is extended and trying to hold a position, or is it most noticeable when you reach for an object and touch it? Additionally, have you noticed any stiffness in your arms or legs, or a feeling that your movements are slower than usual?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's Disease. The clinical picture of a unilateral resting tremor, bradykinesia (soft speech, reduced facial expressions), and early cognitive decline is highly suggestive of this condition.
